newsitem.title: USA: Clinton ready to resume putting practice.
newsitem.headline: Clinton ready to resume putting practice.

text.p: U.S. President Bill Clinton can once again practice his golf putting because his recovery from knee surgery is progressing so well, the White House announced on Tuesday.

"Do not be surprised if you see the president ... putting on the Eisenhower putting green," spokesman Mike McCurry told reporters. "His doctors have concluded that his rehabilitation and recuperation is going sufficiently well."

McCurry was referring to a practice putting green on the White House south lawn within sight of the Oval Office that was installed by Dwight Eisenhower, the most avid presidential duffer until Clinton became commander-in-chief.

"I think the doctors are very happy with the way the leg's healing up. But he has not pushed it and doesn't intend to and doesn't want to get out and test the leg by trying to take a full golf swing any time soon," McCurry said.

Clinton tore a tendon in his right knee in mid-March when he stumbled on a step at the Florida home of Australian golf pro Greg Norman. The injury forced him to undergo emergency surgery, and he is now walking with the aid of a cane after using a wheelchair and crutches for nearly two months.
McCurry said that while Clinton is now able to work on his putting again, he is still a long way away from going out and playing an actual round of golf.
"My guess is it's still going to be fairly late summer before that's even a possibility," the spokesman said.
